articles.content: Announcing Next-Edit in Kilo, Powered by Inception Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in Announcing Next-Edit in Kilo, Powered by Inception With Mercury Edit 2, Next-Edit is Free in Kilo for an Entire Month Ari Messer Jun 22, 2026 5 Share Coding at the speed of thought just got a massive upgrade. Today, we’re thrilled to introduce Next-Edit in Kilo , powered by the Mercury Edit 2 model from Inception . Next-Edit is like a co-editor that predicts what should be coming next based on your recent snippets, file context, and edit history. To celebrate this leap forward, we are making Next-Edit completely free for everyone for the next month . No trials to activate and no credit cards to enter—anytime you use Next-Edit powered by Inception over the next 30 days, it’s completely on us via the Kilo Gateway.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Next-Edit is now the default for new users, but classic autocomplete isn't going anywhere. You get both modes and can switch in a few clicks from settings.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Mercury Edit 2 runs on a diffusion LLM, so it refines edits in parallel instead of left to right one token at a time. Inception's benchmarks: 48% higher edit acceptance, 27% more selective. Fewer interruptions when you're in flow.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: What makes Next-Edit click: it reads your recent edits and codebase context to anticipate what you'll change next. → Refactor a function you just touched → Rename a variable across a block → Cascade a feature change through the file It's a co-editor working alongside you, reaching for the change before you do.

tweets.text: And agents have the following responsibilities/roles: * Planner - researches the objective, writes checkable acceptance criteria * Skeptics - adversarial verifiers; default to refuted * Strategist - fires when stuck (stall / no-progress) * Summarizer - fires once the verified achievement: concise what was delivered + how to use it

tweets.creator: @theskory
tweets.text: The /goal loop is represented in the following way: * Planner subagent → frozen plan.md (acceptance criteria + verification plan) * Implementer rounds (the main model doing work) * Adversarial panel - “skeptic” subagents → Refuted/!Refuted * Continuation directive re-enters the loop until no refutes * Closing summary surfaced to the user

tweets.creator: @theskory
tweets.text: You can opt-out for that behaviour if you only trust your current model. Simply add the following to your grok config (~/.grok/config.toml): [features] goal_use_current_model_only = true
